name: DexYCB: A Benchmark for Capturing Hand Grasping of Objects
description: DexYCB is a multi-view video benchmark and dataset for capturing dexterous human hand grasping of everyday 3D objects. Developed by NVIDIA Research, DexYCB comprises 582,000 synchronized RGB-D video frames recorded across 1,000 grasp execution sequences of 10 human subjects grasping 20 objects from the YCB object set. Captured using an 8-camera multi-sensor calibrated rig, the dataset provides complete 3D hand mesh parameters (fitted to the MANO hand model), ground-truth 6D object poses, and multi-view 2D segmentations to advance 3D hand-object interaction modeling, pose estimation, and dexterous robotic imitation.

size.notes: The full dataset archive (dex-ycb-20210415.tar.gz) is 119 GB via Google Drive, or downloadable as 10 per-subject archives of ~12 GB each.

citation.paper_title: DexYCB: A Benchmark for Capturing Hand Grasping of Objects

provenance.collection_method: Synchronized capture across 8 calibrated RGB-D cameras surrounding seated human subjects performing naturalistic grasps on 20 YCB objects.
provenance.curation_notes: Standardized evaluation protocols include S0 (default), S1 (unseen subjects), S2 (unseen camera views), and S3 (unseen grasping trajectories).
data_sources: Original multi-camera captures at NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab
